title: Deep Depression Nears Odisha Coast; Schools Shut, Landfall Expected Tonight
excerpt: A Bay of Bengal depression is set to intensify and cross between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur on September 23 night, with heavy rain forecast till September 25 — but it is not a cyclone yet.
body:
• A depression over the Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a deep depression and cross the Odisha-Andhra coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur on the night of September 23.
  • Schools and Anganwadi centres are shut across at least nine Odisha districts, with Khordha closed for three days; government employees' leave has been cancelled in the worst-hit areas.
  • The system is NOT yet a cyclone — despite social media chatter about a name, the IMD has not classified or named it, and it remains below cyclonic-storm wind thresholds.
  • Heavy rain is forecast to continue till September 25, with red and orange alerts across eight states and NDRF teams deployed in Odisha.

Odisha is bracing for a landfall. A depression churning over the west-central Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify into a deep depression within hours and cross the north Andhra Pradesh-south Odisha coast between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur on the night of September 23, the India Meteorological Department said on Tuesday. Heavy rain has already lashed coastal and southern Odisha, forcing school closures, the cancellation of government employees' leave, and the deployment of disaster-response teams across vulnerable districts.

Where the system stands

At 8:30 AM IST on Tuesday, the depression lay centred near latitude 17.9°N and longitude 86.0°E — about 200 km southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha, 210 km south of Puri, and 290 km east of Visakhapatnam — moving westwards at 18 kmph, according to the IMD's bulletin. The department said it is "very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a deep depression" over the next 12 hours.

The IMD's own director has said rain is likely to continue in Odisha until September 25, two days past the expected landfall. As of Tuesday, no deaths or major damage had been reported. Koraput and Malkangiri are forecast to receive isolated extremely heavy rainfall, while districts including Khordha and Jagatsinghpur remain under intense-rain warnings. Some areas could receive up to 20 cm of rain, with wind speeds reaching 55 to 65 km/h from Tuesday evening.

Shutdowns and precautions

The state government has moved early. Khordha district — home to the state capital Bhubaneswar — shut all schools for three days from September 22 to 24, covering government, aided, private schools, Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas. Jagatsinghpur, Ganjam and Gajapati closed schools and Anganwadi centres on Tuesday; Malkangiri's closures run through September 24; and Kalahandi, Koraput, Puri and Rayagada ordered closures for Wednesday, September 23. Teachers and staff must still report, with roster duties keeping school buildings accessible around the clock as potential emergency shelters.

The leave of government employees has been cancelled in Ganjam, Koraput and Kalahandi, with officials told not to leave their headquarters. Ferry services between Satapada and Jahnikuda in Chilika Lake will remain suspended till September 25, and vehicular movement has been restricted on roads including the Kalinga Ghat connecting Ganjam and Kandhamal. Dozens of NDRF and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force teams, equipped with boats and rescue gear, have been positioned to evacuate low-lying villages. In Rayagada alone, three permanent multipurpose cyclone shelters and 84 temporary ones have been kept ready, and 11 landslide-vulnerable locations have been identified. Notably, the National Rural Talent Scholarship examination scheduled for September 22 went ahead as planned at 13 designated centres.

Is it a cyclone? Not yet

Social media has been abuzz with claims that a cyclone named "Arnab" is approaching. The facts are more restrained. The system is currently a depression, expected to become a deep depression — both well below the wind-speed threshold at which the IMD names a system. By the department's classification, a depression carries sustained winds of 31–50 kmph and a deep depression 52–61 kmph; only at 63 kmph and above does a system become a cyclonic storm and earn a name. "Arnab" was contributed by Bangladesh to the regional naming list, but treating it as the system's name before the IMD uses it is premature. As one tracker put it: treat any name attached to the system before the IMD itself uses one as unconfirmed.

What's next

The immediate window is the night of September 23 into the early hours of September 24, when the deep depression is expected to cross the coast. Red and orange alerts for heavy rain extend beyond Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to Chhattisgarh, east Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha in Maharashtra, and other states — eight in all — as the system's remnants push inland on September 24 and 25. Authorities have advised citizens to avoid non-essential travel on September 23 and 24, stay clear of weak structures and waterlogged areas, and rely only on official weather bulletins. With rivers already swollen from days of rain, the flood risk in low-lying regions will be the metric to watch once the system makes landfall.
nri_angle: Odia families abroad should check on relatives in coastal and southern districts, where schools are shut and evacuation teams are on standby through September 25.
author: Diaspora Desk
